tools.name: source_route
tools.description: Find likely authoritative or machine-readable sources when you know what information you need but not where to retrieve it. Provide a goal and optional publisher domain or start URL; it returns ranked candidate routes and bounded evidence. Use it before blind searching. Do not use it when you alread

tools.name: error_route
tools.description: Diagnose a failed API, HTTP, MCP, or tool request and return a bounded safe next action. Use it after a request fails when the safe next step is unclear. Provide a status, response, or error text; it does not execute requests or verify undocumented fixes. Price: $0.002 USD per call via x402.

tools.name: request_repair
tools.description: Repair a failed API or HTTP request using only supplied schema and error evidence. Use after error_route identifies a request-shape or input problem. Returns the smallest justified request changes and abstains when evidence is insufficient. Price: $0.005 USD per call via x402.

tools.name: stop_search
tools.description: Decide whether another search or paid retrieval is worth the cost based on the scope already checked. Use after several search or source checks when you need to decide whether to continue or return a scoped not-found result. It does not prove universal absence and performs no searches itself. Price:

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: source_route · Public sink: request_repair · Destructive: error_route.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: source_route · Public sink: request_repair · Destructive: error_route

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
